description: Composite six-panel figure of mechanical data for four low-density δ-ferrite steels, R650, R750, R850 and R950. (a) plots room-temperature impact energy (J, axis 0-250) against rolling temperature (°C) with four error-bar points at 650, 750, 850 and 950 °C; energy collapses from about 207 J at 650 °C to about 80 J at 750 °C and to nearly zero at 850 and 950 °C. (b, c) are instrumented Charpy impact load-displacement curves with dual axes — impact load (kN, 0-20) left, absorbed energy (J, 0-250) right, displacement (mm) bottom; (b) covers R650 and R750 out to 24 mm with printed annotations Ep = 147.90 J and Ei = 92.93 J (R650) and Ei = 50.14 J, Ep = 51.51 J (R750); (c) covers R850 and R950 over only 0-5 mm with printed Ei = 3.91 J, Ep = 2.10 J (R850) and Ei = 2.95 J, Ep = 2.29 J (R950), showing steep single peaks near 17 and 6 kN that decay within ~1 mm. (d) shows engineering stress-strain curves (MPa vs %): R950 (green) and R850 (blue) reach the highest stress at small strain; R750 (red) and R650 (black) the largest elongation. (e) plots work-hardening rate versus true strain for R650 and R750, both with a hump near true strain 0.03-0.04; (f) shows monotonic decay for R850 and R950. The panels jointly demonstrate that low-temperature rolling gives strength-plasticity synergy through a sustained work-hardening hump, whereas high-temperature rolling causes brittle single-peak impact failure.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots impact energy (J, 0-250 axis) against rolling temperature (℃) at four temperatures 650, 750, 850 and 950, all with error bars; the value drops steeply between 650 and 850 °C and is nearly zero at 850 and 950 °C.

The caption identifies the tested steels as R650, R750, R850 and R950 and assigns (a) room-temperature impact energy absorption, (b, c) impact load-displacement curves, (d) engineering stress-strain curves under room-temperature tension, and (e, f) work-hardening rate curves.
Panel (b) prints Ep = 147.90 J and Ei = 92.93 J for R650, and Ei = 50.14 J and Ep = 51.51 J for R750, on a load axis of 0-20 kN and an absorbed-energy axis of 0-250 J.

The citing text states the R650 crack initiation energy Ei is 59.6 J and Ep is 147.9 J, which conflicts with the Ei = 92.93 J printed inside panel (b); both readings are reported, the discrepancy is not resolved by the pixels.
Panel (c) prints Ei = 3.91 J and Ep = 2.10 J for R850 and Ei = 2.95 J and Ep = 2.29 J for R950, with a displacement axis of only 0-5 mm.
Both curves in panel (c) are steep single peaks that decay to near zero load within roughly 1 mm displacement, unlike the long R650 plateau in panel (b) that extends to about 14 mm.
The citing text reports room-temperature impact absorption energies of 207.5 ± 29.3 J (R650), 75.9 ± 22.3 J (R750), 5.6 ± 0.6 J (R850) and 4.6 ± 0.2 J (R950), consistent with the trend of panel (a).

Panel (d) legends four engineering stress-strain curves (R650, R750, R850, R950) over Stress 0-1400 MPa and Strain 0-25 %; strength increases and elongation decreases with increasing rolling temperature.
The citing text states tensile strength rises from 868.7 MPa in R650 to 1254.5 MPa in R950 while the strength-plasticity product falls from 16.51 to 4.4 GPa·%.
The citing text gives elongations of 19.0 ± 3.2 % (R650), 17.3 ± 3.6 % (R750), 8.3 ± 0.1 % (R850) and 3.5 ± 0.8 % (R950), matching the strain extents of the four curves in panel (d).

Panel (e) shows two work-hardening-rate curves versus true strain (0-0.15) for R650 (black) and R750 (red); both display a trough followed by a hump at moderate strain (roughly 0.03-0.04) before decaying.
Panel (f) shows work-hardening-rate curves versus true strain (0-0.08) for R850 (black) and R950 (red) that decrease monotonically with no rising hump.

The citing text attributes the hump in the work-hardening curve of the low-temperature rolled specimen to Orowan pinning of dislocations by carbides (<250 nm diameter) in the ferrite/carbide composite lamellae, whereas the high-temperature rolled specimens show a monotonically decreasing curve.
In panel (a) the error bar at 650 °C spans roughly from 175 to 235 J and the one at 750 °C roughly from 60 to 100 J, while the 850 and 950 °C error bars are too small to resolve at this rendering.

subfigures.description: Line plot of Impact Energy (J), y-axis 0-250 in 50 J steps, versus Rolling temperature (℃) with four data points at 650, 750, 850 and 950 °C, each with vertical error bars. The value is near 207 J at 650 °C, falls to ~80 J at 750 °C, and is essentially zero (~5 J) at 850 and 950 °C.

Instrumented Charpy impact load-displacement curves for R650 (solid, upper curve) and R750 (dashed) plotted on dual axes: Impact Load (kN) 0-20 on the left, Absorbed Energy (J) 0-250 on the right, Displacement (mm) 0-24 on the bottom. Printed annotations: R650 Ep = 147.90 J and Ei = 92.93 J; R750 Ei = 50.14 J and Ep = 51.51 J. R650 retains load over a long plateau/rise out to ~14 mm displacement; R750 falls away earlier.

Impact load-displacement curves for R850 and R950, same dual axes (Impact Load (kN) 0-20; Absorbed Energy (J) 0-250) but displacement only 0-5 mm. Printed annotations: R850 Ei = 3.91 J, Ep = 2.10 J; R950 Ei = 2.95 J, Ep = 2.29 J. Both curves are steep single peaks (R850 reaching roughly 17 kN, R950 roughly 6 kN) that drop to near zero within about 1 mm of displacement.

Engineering stress-strain curves under room-temperature tension, Stress (MPa) 0-1400 versus Strain (%) 0-25, with legend R650, R750, R850 and R950. The R950 (green) and R850 (blue) curves reach the highest stresses at the smallest strains, while R650 (black) shows a long plateau near ~860 MPa with the largest elongation and R750 (red) the lowest plateau of the four.

Work-hardening rate (θ, y-axis 0-5000) versus True Strain (0.00-0.15) for R650 (black) and R750 (red). Both curves fall steeply at low strain, pass through a minimum, then show a distinct hump (R650 peaking near true strain 0.035 at ~2400, R750 near 0.03 at ~2700) before decaying.

Work-hardening rate (y-axis 0-~35000, top tick label partially clipped) versus True Strain (0.00-0.08) for R850 (black) and R950 (red). Both curves decrease monotonically from above ~30000 at very low strain with no hump; R850 extends to about 0.08 true strain while R950 stops near 0.035.

unreadable_items: panel (f): the highest y-axis tick label of the work-hardening rate axis is partially clipped/overlapped by the '(f)' marker, so its exact value cannot be read

panel (b): the solid versus dashed curve assignment for the R650/R750 pair is stated in coloured text (R650 blue, R750 blue) but the curves themselves are black/grey, so which trace belongs to which specimen at overlapping displacements is only inferred from the annotations
panel (c): the small low-load oscillations after the main peak cannot be resolved into distinct labelled events
